basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 2:15 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 51. Quid est, quod dixit [ Ms., dicitur]: Et posuit Deus hominem in paradiso'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 51. Quid est, quod dixit [ Ms., dicitur]: Et posuit Deus hominem in paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur et custodiret illum (Gen. II, 15)? [Nunquid homini laborare in paradiso opus fuit]; aut a quo custodire illum [ Edit., illud; al. custodiri ille] debuit?-- Resp. Non enim [homini erat] laboris afflictio in paradiso, sed voluntatis exhilaratio; cum ea quae Deus creaverat humani operis adjutorio laetius feraciusque [ Ms., veracius] provenirent. Et custodiret illum, ut custodiret eumdem paradisum sibi ipsi, et [ Ms., ne] si aliquid amitteret, ut inde mereretur expelli.
